rows.citation: Patten-Elliott, F., Lei, C. L., Preston, S. P., et al. (2025). Optimizing experimental designs for model selection of ion channel drug-binding mechanisms. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences, 383(2292).
rows.model_type: Cardiac hERG ion-channel Markov ODE models (Lei and Lu hERG models) combined with 15 candidate drug-binding mechanism models, simulated in Myokit under voltage clamp
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - compares 15 structurally distinct candidate drug-binding models plus a discrepant hERG model; competing hypotheses, not recorded single-fault mutants of a reference model.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - contrasts a modified Milnes voltage-clamp protocol with one optimized two-pulse protocol; voltage clamp only, no current-clamp battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - discrimination uses pairwise sum-of-squares differences between simulated traces and maximized log-likelihoods of fits, not extracted electrophysiological features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - CMA-ES maximizes the median pairwise trace difference between candidate models over eight voltage and timing protocol parameters.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - robustness examined with a discrepant data-generating hERG model and several drugs; no discovery/held-out model or mutation-family split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted model editing or transformation is studied.
rows.software: binding_model_OED - https://github.com/CardiacModelling/binding_model_OED (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API); paper also cites a Zenodo archive 10.5281/zenodo.14751331 (not resolved here)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest electrophysiology precedent for designing stimuli that separate model variants. NeuroSem instead detects post-edit drift in NeuroML neurons: fixed current-clamp protocol library, eFEL features, refinement-calibrated tolerances, greedy subset selection over mutants, held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (api.crossref.org/works/10.1098/rsta.2024.0227: title, 5 authors, volume 383 issue 2292, 2025-03-13, CC BY 4.0); Europe PMC search (PMID 40078143, PMC11904620) and full-text XML read (methods, max-med criterion, discrepancy section, data accessibility); GitHub REST API for repo and license; bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2024.08.20.608856 confirmed on Crossref as posted-content with same authors.

rows.citation: Matinnejad, R., Nejati, S., Briand, L. C., et al. (2016). Automated test suite generation for time-continuous Simulink models. Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Software Engineering, pp. 595-606.
rows.model_type: Time-continuous Simulink controller models (industrial automotive models from Delphi plus public-domain models); cyber-physical systems, not neuroscience
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - automated fault seeding from Simulink fault patterns produced 104 executable faulty model versions, one fault per model, used to measure fault revealing ability.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - generates small test suites (size 3, 5, 10) of piecewise input signals per model.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - feature-based output diversity uses signal-shape features (e.g. increasing, instability, discontinuity); analogous to trace features but not electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - meta-heuristic whole-suite search maximizes output-signal diversity at fixed suite size; compared with random testing and Simulink Design Verifier.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - search is fault-agnostic and run on each faulty model; no discovery/held-out model or fault-family split reported.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-assisted model transformations.
rows.software: SimCoTest - https://sites.google.com/site/simcotesttool/ (URL as cited in the TSE 2019 follow-up; not checked live); ICSE resources https://sites.google.com/site/myicseresources/ (cited in paper, not checked)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Strong SE analogue: small fault-revealing input suites for continuous models with seeded faults. NeuroSem uses a fixed interpretable neuroscience protocol library, eFEL features with calibrated tolerances against a reference model, mutant-coverage greedy selection, and held-out models/family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 4 authors, ICSE 38 proceedings, pp. 595-606, 2016-05-14); Semantic Scholar Graph API and OpenAlex (abstract, DBLP key conf/icse/MatinnejadNBB16); open-access technical report PDF from ORBilu (orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/21975/1/TR.pdf) read for experiment design and fault seeding.
rows.found_via: WebSearch 'Simulink model test generation output diversity fault revealing mutants Matinnejad'; metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works | WebSearch site:dl.acm.org test selection simulation models cyber-physical Simulink mutation; OpenAlex search 'mutation analysis Simulink test selection'; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Matinnejad, R., Nejati, S., Briand, L. C., et al. (2019). Test Generation and Test Prioritization for Simulink Models with Dynamic Behavior. IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, 45(9), 919-944.
rows.model_type: Industrial Simulink models with dynamic (time-varying) behaviour from Delphi Automotive; cyber-physical systems, not neuroscience
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - automated fault-seeding program applies mutation operators derived from Simulink fault patterns to model elements; 74 faulty models evaluated, plus three real faults reported.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - search generates test suites of input signals (sizes 3, 5, 10) per model output.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - feature-based output diversity over signal-shape features; generic signal features, not electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - diversity-driven search generation plus greedy budget-oriented test prioritization; compared with random and coverage-based generation and prioritization.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - evaluated on seeded faulty versions of the subject models; no discovery/held-out model or fault-family split found in retrieved text.
rows.software: SimCoTest - https://sites.google.com/site/simcotesttool/ ; paper resources https://github.com/shnejati/TSE-Master (both as cited in paper; not checked live)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest SE work combining stimulus generation, budgeted greedy ranking and seeded faults. Its ranking uses surrogate diversity/coverage rewards with manual oracles; NeuroSem selects by known mutant detection with tolerance-calibrated automatic oracles, for NeuroML neurons, validated on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 4 authors, TSE 45(9):919-944, issued 2019-09-01; OpenAlex lists publication year 2018, online-first); Semantic Scholar Graph API and OpenAlex abstract; open-access author version from ORBilu (orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/35029/1/paper.pdf) read for fault seeding, RQs, prioritization algorithm and tool references.
rows.found_via: Crossref title query (after WebSearch on Matinnejad Simulink test generation); metadata verified via Crossref api.crossref.org/works | WebSearch site:dl.acm.org test selection simulation models cyber-physical Simulink mutation; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Kavak, M., Kilincceker, O., Demeyer, S., et al. (2026). Mutation Testing of Simulink Cyber-Physical System Models: Challenges and Solutions in Practice. arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.24250.
rows.model_type: Industrial Simulink/Stateflow control models for building ventilation systems (three pilot models); cyber-physical systems, not neuroscience
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - MUT4SLX operators (28 Simulink, 18 Stateflow) generated 459 mutants across three models; equivalent mutants identified manually and partly filtered.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - existing unit test cases (Signal Builder input scenarios) scored individually and as whole suites; no new stimulus design.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - mutants counted killed when test assertions trigger; no signal feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - reports single-test-case versus full-suite mutation scores but proposes no test selection or minimization algorithm.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - experience report on a pilot project; no held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - LLM-based Simulink mutant generation by others appears only in related work.
rows.software: MUT4SLX (tool named in paper; no public repository URL found in retrieved text)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares the equivalent-mutant problem that NeuroSem handles via admissibility classification. NeuroSem addresses equivalence empirically (exhaustive battery, refinement tolerances) for neuron models and adds feature fingerprints, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page (arxiv.org/abs/2608.24250: citation meta tags, 5 authors, submitted 2026-08-25, comments state acceptance at ASE 2026); DataCite API for 10.48550/arXiv.2608.24250; arXiv PDF read (RQs, mutant counts, equivalent-mutant section). arXiv export API returned 'Rate exceeded'. ACM DOI 10.1145/3832783.3834529 listed on arXiv page is not found on Crossref and doi.org handle API returned not found on 2026-09-13, so arXiv DOI is used.

rows.model_type: Stochastic biophysical spiking network simulation (feedforward multisensory network case study)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - abstract reports detecting structural mismatches before analysis but describes no mutation operators; full text not retrieved.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract does not describe stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - applies batch-level stochastic regression criteria to simulation outputs; specific features not stated in abstract.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol or test selection described in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - single network case study per abstract.
rows.software: none found (abstract names the NeuroCERT testing layer; no repository URL retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares motivation of regression testing neuroscience simulations with weak oracles. NeuroCERT stresses provenance, pre-run structural checks and stochastic network outputs; NeuroSem targets deterministic NeuroML neurons with single-fault mutants, multi-protocol eFEL fingerprints, calibrated tolerances, battery selection and held-out evaluation.

rows.citation: Sarma, G. P., Jacobs, T. W., Watts, M. D., et al. (2016). Unit testing, model validation, and biological simulation. F1000Research, 5, 1946.
rows.model_type: Biological simulation software (OpenWorm C. elegans project, including ion-channel models in ChannelWorm and PyOpenWorm data)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - discusses unit tests, test-driven development and continuous integration; no mutation or fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - example NeuronUnit test checks one ion channel's I/V curve against data; no multi-protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - SciUnit model validation tests compute summary statistics (e.g. I/V peak agreement) mapped to pass/fail scores.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no stimulus or test selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - case-study/perspective article without quantitative evaluation.
rows.software: SciUnit http://sciunit.scidash.org ; NeuronUnit http://neuronunit.scidash.org ; ChannelWorm https://github.com/openworm/ChannelWorm (URLs as cited in paper)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Conceptual precedent for model validation tests inside CI. NeuroSem instead tests regression against a reference model rather than agreement with data, adding controlled mutants, multi-protocol fingerprints, calibrated tolerances, compact battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (title, 6 authors, F1000Research 5:1946, 2016-08-10, CC BY 4.0); Europe PMC search (PMID 27635225, PMC5007758) and full-text XML read (test categories, SciUnit/NeuronUnit example, CI section).
